correctness.rationale: The thirteen projective sign-pattern points account for all 36 line pairs (6 double, 4 triple, 3 quadruple), with no change in the declared characteristic. The seven blowups give a connected 16-vertex, 30-edge dual graph of minimum degree three, so the rational components give a stable genus-15 curve. The normalization units sequence identifies the character lattice as the kernel of the integral incidence map, not just the rational cycle representation. Independent reconstruction in /workspace/branches/check5.py used the sign-pattern points, directed graph edges, leaf-to-root cycle lifting and exact rational elimination to check all five integral basis certificates with the supplied seeds; determinants are 1, 1, -1, 1, -1. The five representatives act on the long diagonals with the asserted cycle types and sizes. No edge orientation is reversed, so each node orbit contributes two branch orbits of the same length. A fixed component of the normalization contributes q^r+1 points over F_(q^r) (a finite-field form of P^1 is split); subtracting fixed branches and adding fixed nodes yields the stated zeta products for every extension degree. The integral regular and sign blocks give the displayed restriction and norm-one tori and their cyclic groups of points. The two involutions have different fixed lattice ranks, and the other three actions have different orders. This does not classify twists by any additional abstract automorphisms.
residual_risks: The assertion is only for characteristic greater than three and the five classes of the specified projective action.

evidence: Geisser gives a general equivariant integral description of the Picard torus; Casalaina-Martin–Kass–Viviani use dual graphs for the local geometry of compactified Jacobians.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general constructions apply or provide context, but leave the specific integral Z[F]-module evaluation and fixed component/node enumeration to be done.

evidence: The graph-theoretic Picard theorem identifies which lattice to compute, but does not provide a unimodular orbit-block basis for this incidence pattern. A rational character cannot distinguish Z[C2] from Z plus the sign lattice, although they imply different integral tori.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The same B3 equation, a prior case with the same S4 parameter set, or a rational-character calculation cannot supply the integral decomposition or the evaluated zeta table without new object-specific checks.

evidence: The nine-line B3 equations agree with the arrangement dualized in arXiv:1804.03610; the dual unexpected quartic is not the resolved nodal divisor. The Cayley calculation instead starts with the nine lines on a cubic surface, with a 22-vertex branch-incidence graph and rank-nine torus.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Neither projective dualization of the nine lines nor rephrasing the Cayley invariant as a graph torus identifies it with this rank-fifteen character lattice.

evidence: The Heawood table uses a 14-vertex incidence graph and GL(3,2) twists; the Igusa calculation treats a 15-line boundary with an S6 action and an integral five-cycle case; the Cayley table has five S4 types but dimension nine.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are evaluated nearby tables rather than the five rank-fifteen integral types of the resolved B3 arrangement.

originality.rationale: The arrangement, Picard-lattice formalism and close arithmetic analogues are established. The inspected evidence does not cover the integral cycle actions and zeta functions for this resolved plane B3 divisor. The same-day Cayley nine-line calculation was compared on its merits, not excluded by date. This is an evidence-bounded decision, not a claim of historical priority.
residual_risks: Equivalent integral matrices or invariant decompositions in differently indexed arrangement literature were not excluded. No historical priority is inferred from the same-day record dates.

value.rationale: The canonical reflection arrangement and its full prescribed geometric symmetry group motivate a complete arithmetic classification, rather than a class selected after computation. For this genus-15 curve the integral table differentiates restriction and norm-one factors that an eigenvalue table does not determine individually. It supplies explicit torus isomorphism types, their finite rational-point groups, and extension-degree counts for every specified twist, useful as exact data for comparison with other arithmetic graph curves.
residual_risks: No general classification of resolved arrangements, all forms, or smoothing invariants follows.
